slot.brief: Probability of drawing cards/balls with at least one condition satisfied; use total minus invalid or direct counting of favourable outcomes.

stem: Two cards are drawn without replacement from a standard $52$-card deck. What is the probability that at least one is an ace or a king?

verdicts.working: Use the complement: neither card is an ace nor a king with probability \(\binom{44}{2}/\binom{52}{2}\). Thus the required probability is \(1-946/1326=190/663\), option C.

working:
$P(\text{at least one ace or king})=1-\dfrac{\binom{44}{2}}{\binom{52}{2}}=1-\dfrac{946}{1326}=\dfrac{190}{663}$.

Independent check: Use the complement: neither card is an ace nor a king with probability \(\binom{44}{2}/\binom{52}{2}\). Thus the required probability is \(1-946/1326=190/663\), option C.
